skill.name: daftai-cloudflare-billing-audit
skill.description: Audits a Cloudflare application repository offline for code paths and configuration that may create usage-based billing exposure. Use when asked to inspect Cloudflare Worker, D1, Durable Objects, storage, queue, or compute usage for unexpected bills, billing risks, or cost drivers. Reports evidence and uncertainty; it does not access an account or guarantee a spending cap.
skill.summary: Review local Cloudflare code and configuration for evidence-linked billing exposure without account access or target-code execution.
skill.author: daftai2026

content.value_statement: Cloudflare applications can accumulate usage charges through retries, recurring jobs, and unbounded work. This skill reviews local configuration and source for supported cost mechanisms and uncertainties.
actual_capabilities: Inventory bounded Wrangler JSON, JSONC, and Bun-supported TOML configuration, including entry points, environments, bindings, trigger counts, and CPU limits.
Generate lexical candidates for recurring Durable Object alarms, queue retries, consumer sends, and looped scheduling or queue sends.
Retrieve listed JavaScript, TypeScript, selected D1 SQL, and GitHub workflow evidence through bounded reads with content and identity fingerprint checks.
Guide source review from configured triggers to chargeable operations, including guard scope, persistence, retries, fan-out, and stopping conditions.
Relate observed usage to product-specific Cloudflare evidence while separating local configuration, deployment uncertainty, and unverified traffic assumptions.
Produce human-readable and machine-readable reports separating scanner candidates, verified conclusions, coverage limits, and follow-up questions.
limitations: Does not access Cloudflare accounts, verify invoices or deployment state, modify settings, or guarantee a spending cap.
The scanner is lexical, not a complete analyzer; call graphs, dynamic dispatch, unsupported syntax, and skipped files require explicit uncertainty.
Requires Bun and supported filesystem access; macOS and Windows adapters require stable trees and do not isolate hostile concurrent mutations.
Default limits are 500 files, 4,000 entries, and 2 MiB total; monetary estimates require separately requested, current official pricing and usage assumptions.

use_cases.title: Review a Worker before release
use_cases.description: Inspect configured request paths and recurring jobs for source-supported cost amplification before deployment.

use_cases.title: Investigate queue and alarm exposure
use_cases.description: Trace queue feedback, retries, and Durable Object scheduling while distinguishing persistent job limits from per-invocation controls.

use_cases.title: Prepare a cost-risk review
use_cases.description: Summarize supported mechanisms, coverage gaps, and owner verification steps without requiring credentials or assuming production usage.

prompt_templates.title: Start an offline audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the Cloudflare project at [absolute project path] for billing exposure. Keep the review offline and read-only, and separate supported findings from unknowns.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on one workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [absolute workspace path] for Workers and D1 cost mechanisms. Review configured entry points, query amplification, and listed migrations. Record deployment and index uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Trace recurring work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [absolute project path] for queue feedback and Durable Object alarm recurrence. Trace persistent job budgets, progress, retries, and terminal guards through fingerprint-checked evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: recurring jobs and feedback paths

prompt_templates.title: Model a bounded cost scenario
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [absolute project path] and estimate costs using [plan, period, currency, and supplied usage assumptions]. Retrieve current official pricing and record dates, units, and uncertainties.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: review a consumer that sends follow-on messages to its own queue.
output: Conditional exposure: a successful message can create another message, extending work beyond a single delivery retry limit.
Verify a persistent root-job budget, advancing progress, deduplication, and terminal handling before classifying the path as bounded.
Production routing, invocation volume, and actual charges remain unknown without separately supplied evidence.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: audit a repository where a required source file exceeds the read limit.
output: Coverage is partial: the oversized file was excluded from source review.
The affected trigger chain remains unknown; no conclusion relies on the excluded contents.
Request a narrower supported review scope instead of bypassing the controlled reader.

best_practices: Provide an explicit project path and a private output location outside the target tree; keep target, ancestor, and output trees stable.
Review only fingerprint-checked evidence and inspect actual triggers, guards, and persistent limits before promoting a scanner candidate.
Keep traffic assumptions, deployment uncertainty, and pricing dates explicit; use current official pricing only for requested estimates.
anti_patterns: Treating an empty candidate list or a binding declaration as proof of safety or proof of a billing defect.
Running target scripts, reading excluded credential files, or bypassing a refused controlled read with another reader.
Presenting budget alerts, per-request limits, or stale pricing as a guaranteed whole-account spending cap.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Its helper requires Bun and a supported local filesystem environment.

faq.question: Does the audit require a Cloudflare token?
faq.answer: No. Default audits inspect local files offline and do not sign in, call account APIs, or read credentials.

faq.question: Does it run or modify my application?
faq.answer: No. It does not execute target code, scripts, tests, hooks, or migrations. Reports are written outside the target tree.

faq.question: Can it prevent an unexpected bill?
faq.answer: No. It identifies supported exposure mechanisms and review gaps. It does not enforce account limits or guarantee a spending cap.

faq.question: Are all Cloudflare products scanned automatically?
faq.answer: No. Automated candidates cover narrow alarm and queue patterns. Product guides support broader agent review of authorized evidence.

faq.question: Can it estimate monthly charges?
faq.answer: Only when explicitly requested. Estimates require current official prices, plan details, billing period, currency, usage assumptions, and stated uncertainties.
